reference_role: User-supplied graphic dragon style; simplified further and integrated with a code-rendered grid.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: transparent graphic dragon for JeRyū's futuristic landing page.
Input image: supplied image is a STYLE reference: flowing cyan/blue/violet graphic ribbons and elegant Japanese dragon, not a background to preserve.
Primary request: redesign this as a MUCH CLEANER, less busy, powerful GRAPHIC illustration of ONE Japanese digital dragon racing toward the RIGHT. A confident streamlined dragon, head in the upper-right looking forward/right, one connected serpentine S-shaped body descending through the composition into one tapered tail. Its mane and tail ribbons sweep strongly to the LEFT, as though moving fast into the future. This is bold graphic design, not a realistic scaly creature.
Style/medium: polished vector-like illustration with large clean silhouettes, broad flowing ribbons and restrained gradient planes. Use about 8–12 large mane/tail ribbons, minimal scale indication (a few large facets), a clean continuous pearl belly, no tiny hairs or individually rendered dense scales. Readable at thumbnail size, graceful negative space through the body curve.
Palette: luminous cyan and electric cobalt, small indigo/violet accents, pearl-white belly and two elegant pearl horns, deep navy contour shapes. Make cyan highlights pop without excessive neon bloom. No red.
Anatomy: exactly one head, one continuous body and one tail, TWO main horns with no extra horn/spike growing out of the mane. Two small anatomically attached forelegs, each with three clear claws; coherent joints, no detached claws or extra limbs. One fine, tapered whisker on either side of the muzzle, similar relative length adjusted slightly for perspective, swept backward to the left in the slipstream; no loops or knotted noodles. Fierce elegant expression and one bright cyan near eye, far eye only if anatomically visible.
Composition: portrait 3:4, full dragon visible with generous transparent breathing room on ALL sides including every whisker, horn and tail tip. The shape should feel accelerating to the right while remaining a tall S composition for the right side of a website. Do not add graphic strokes that could be mistaken for another serpent body.
Scene/backdrop: ACTUAL TRANSPARENT ALPHA background. Only the dragon cutout. Remove ALL reference grid lines, circuit nodes, circles, ornamental dots, particles, speed streaks and background objects; those will be animated separately in code. No backdrop, floor, frame, text, letters, logo or watermark. Preserve crisp clean alpha edges and do not bake in a rectangle or checkerboard.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Edit target: the attached transparent graphic Japanese dragon. Keep its broad flowing graphic ribbons, forward/right-facing pose, one continuous S-shaped body, one tail, two main pearl horns, cyan/cobalt/indigo/pearl palette and simplified clean planes unchanged.
Fix the framing: the current tips hit the canvas edges. Zoom the ENTIRE dragon out about 18% on the same 3:4 portrait canvas and center it so every horn, mane ribbon, nose, claw, whisker and tail tip has at least 7% clear transparent margin on every side. Reconstruct any clipped tips naturally. Do not crop any physical part of the dragon.
Fix whisker balance: the visible long cyan filament extending left from the near muzzle is much too long. Shorten it to about half its current length, a graceful thin open backward-swept curve with a tapered free tip. Both whiskers should have approximately comparable lengths, allowing the near one to be at most 25% longer in perspective. Both should attach naturally once to opposite sides of the muzzle, neither should loop or reattach.
Refine cutout edges: remove stray grainy cyan specks and pixel-noise halo around the silhouette, leaving clean smooth graphic alpha edges. Preserve controlled luminous edge color inside the actual illustration.
Keep coherent connected legs and clearly separated claws. Exactly one head, one body, one tail, two main horns. Do not add horns or extra limbs. Keep the broad bold graphic style; do not add dense scales, fine hair, dots, circles, circuits, speed lines, text or any background. ACTUAL TRANSPARENT ALPHA.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Edit target: this transparent graphic dragon. Change ONLY the dragon's whiskers.
There is an unwanted thin loop floating in front of the nose, and a long cyan filament floating across the mane away from the muzzle. Remove ALL those thin filaments and loops completely, repairing the underlying broad mane shapes.
Give the dragon exactly TWO SMALL elegant whiskers. Both grow visibly from opposite corners of the MUZZLE beside the nose, sweep BACKWARD to the LEFT, and end in free tapered tips. Each is only about the length of the dragon's muzzle (nose to eye), approximately 90–120 pixels on this image. The near whisker can be slightly longer, but no more than 20%. Use thin pearl-cyan strokes, no large loops, no reattachment, no curled forward filament beyond the nose. The whiskers must be clearly anatomical, with visible attachment to the muzzle and clear pointed free ends.
Everything else stays identical: simplified broad graphic ribbon style, right-facing head, two pearl horns, one continuous S body and one tail, connected legs/claws, cyan/cobalt/indigo/pearl colors, exact full-body framing and transparent margins. Do not add fine hair, extra body parts, extra horns, dots, background lines or any backdrop. Preserve actual transparent alpha.

review.style: Broad graphic ribbons and large planes, minimal scale marks, no dense hairs or baked circuit ornaments.
review.body: One connected S-shaped spine and continuous pearl belly flows into one tail; two connected forelimbs with separated claws.
review.horns: Two pearl main horns; no extra blue horn-like spike.
review.whiskers: Two open pearl-cyan backward-swept filaments on a comparable scale; no forward closed loop.
review.direction: Head faces right; broad mane and tail sweep left in the slipstream.
review.alpha: Genuine RGBA transparency; full physical anatomy inside the frame. Export hashes and dimensions are recorded by the declared Node generator.
review.framing: 1086 x 1448; substantial alpha bbox (89,57,1057,1433); all physical tips inside the frame, bottom margin 15px, right margin 29px. Edge alpha maximum is 0 except a trace alpha value of 1 at left; no physical clipping.
